tool_input.description: Inspect JSON dictionary entries for key variables

result:
All nine files are written to `out/` and validated. Every JSON file parses, every claim's target references resolve, the spec-space origin and manifest open decisions cross-check, and the manifest scan found no identity, published N, or result-direction content (the only flagged strings are the d formula and its sign convention, which the schema requires).

**Summary of what I produced.** From the single packet document (P1, 26 PDF pages) and the summary-free MTF dictionaries, I built a claim map of 59 claims (13 focal latent-mean comparisons across the five work-value factors for the three year pairs, 9 identification/inference diagnostics covering the CFA, alpha-based item dropping and the five-step invariance sequence, and 37 descriptive claims including one per Table 1 item); a sealed targets file with 534 transcribed numbers (all Table 1 means, SDs, percentages, t statistics, latent means, SEs, CIs and d values; all Table 2 fit statistics and nested-model differences; form and total Ns; text-only figures) with stars recorded as inequalities and nothing filled from memory; a target-free manifest for PAPER_X mapping the 23 Form 4 and 6 Form 3 items to their exact source variables in the six year-form files (1976 DS0003/DS0004, 1991 DS0004/DS0005, 2006 DS0004/DS0005), with coding, per-release missing codes, construct membership, the six freed intercepts, ordered sample steps, estimator formulas including d as later-minus-earlier over the equal-weight pooled SD, and nine open decisions; a separate published-N branch; a specification space with nine axes (sample/missingness, weighting, d denominator, SD definition, latent-mean scaling, CFA estimator, t-test variant, and two diagnostic item-assignment axes), each with a closest-described origin and sourced labels; documentation and inference assessments; and 18 forensic findings. The forensics confirm that all 15 d values and all 15 confidence intervals reproduce from the printed means, SDs and SEs, and that model df and the total N reconcile, but they also flag a metric-invariance chi-square the text calls nonsignificant that has p of about .043, sign reversals in five item-level t values, one wrong star level, a four-category instrument described as five-point, promised reliabilities absent from Table 1, a partial-invariance rule violated for the altruistic factor, and multigroup df that cannot be reconstructed from the described model. reader_notes.md lists these contradictions, the vintage and weight uncertainties, and coordinator questions. Sixteen targets (participation-rate ranges, RMSEA/SRMSR/TLI for invariance Models 2 to 5, and two cited cutoffs) are transcribed but not linked to a claim; I left the files as first written rather than revise them.
